title.zh: 卷四十六 列傳第十六 劉頌 李重
title.en: Volume 46 Biographies 16: Liu Song; Li Zhong
title.raw: 卷四十六 列傳第十六 劉頌 李重 Volume 46 Biographies 16: Liu Song; Li Zhong

sentences.zh: 劉頌

translations.literal: Liu Song.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 劉頌，字子雅，廣陵人，漢廣陵厲王胥之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, was a man of Guangling, a descendant of the Han Prince Li of Guangling, Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, came from Guangling and traced his line to Prince Li of Guangling under the Han, Liu Xu.

sentences.zh: 世為名族。

translations.literal: For generations they were a famous clan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had ranked among the great houses of the region.

sentences.zh: 同郡有雷、蔣、谷、魯四姓，皆出其下，時人為之語曰「雷、蔣、谷、魯，劉最為祖。

translations.literal: In the same commandery were the four surnames Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu; all came out below them, and people of the time made a saying for them: "Lei, Jiang, Gu, Lu—Liu is most the ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Guangling also boasted the four houses of Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu, yet all stood beneath the Lius, and a local rhyme ran, Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu bow to Liu as their elder stock.

sentences.zh: 」父觀，平陽太守。

translations.literal: " His father Guan was Administrator of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Guan had served as prefect of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 頌少能辨物理，為時人所稱。

translations.literal: Song in youth was able to discriminate things' principles, and was praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Liu Song could reason to the root of affairs and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，舉秀才，皆不就。

translations.literal: He was investigated as filial and incorrupt, recommended as flourishing talent, all did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Though nominated as filial and incorrupt and as a flourishing talent, he declined each summons.

sentences.zh: 文帝辟為相府掾，奉使於蜀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen summoned him as a clerk in the chancellery and sent him on mission to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen appointed him a staff clerk in the princely chancellery and dispatched him on embassy to Shu.

sentences.zh: 時蜀新平，人饑土荒，頌表求振貸，不待報而行，由是除名。

translations.literal: At that time Shu was newly pacified; people starved and the land lay waste. Song memorialized requesting relief loans, without awaiting reply acted, thereby was removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had only just been pacified: the people were starving and the fields lay waste. Liu Song submitted an urgent plea for grain relief and distributed aid before imperial approval arrived, for which he was struck from office.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，拜尚書三公郎，典科律，申冤訟。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was appointed Gentlemen of the Three Excellencies in the Masters of Writing, in charge of statutes and regulations, extending wronged lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne Liu Song was named a Three Excellencies gentleman in the Masters of Writing, charged with statutes and codes and with redressing unjust suits.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to gentleman attendant of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 咸寧中，詔頌與散騎郎白褒巡撫荊、揚，以奉使稱旨，轉黃門郎。

translations.literal: In the Xianning era an edict ordered Song together with Cavalier Gentleman Bai Bao to tour and comfort Jing and Yang; because carrying out the mission matched the intent, he was transferred to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianning the court sent Liu Song and Bai Bao, cavalier gentleman, on an inspection tour of Jingzhou and Yangzhou. The mission pleased the throne, and Liu Song was moved to gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 遷議郎，守廷尉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Consultant and acted as Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to consultant and served as acting commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令史扈寅非罪下獄，詔使考竟，頌執據無罪，寅遂得免，時人以頌比張釋之。

translations.literal: At that time Masters of Writing clerk Hu Yin entered prison without crime; an edict ordered him interrogated to the end. Song held proof of innocence, and Yin was able to be spared. People of the time compared Song to Zhang Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Yin, a clerk of the Masters of Writing, was jailed on a false charge and the emperor ordered a full inquest, Liu Song proved his innocence and secured his release. Contemporaries likened him to the Han jurist Zhang Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 在職六年，號為詳平。

translations.literal: In office six years, he was titled thorough and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Six years in the post earned him a reputation for meticulous fairness.

sentences.zh: 會滅吳，諸將爭功，遣頌校其事，以王渾為上功，王浚為中功。

translations.literal: When Wu was destroyed, the various generals disputed merit; Song was sent to examine the matter, taking Wang Hun as upper merit and Wang Jun as middle merit.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Wu the generals wrangled over credit. The court charged Liu Song with adjudicating their claims; he ranked Wang Hun first and Wang Jun second.

sentences.zh: 帝以頌持法失理，左遷京兆太守，不行，轉任河內。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Song upholding law missed principle, demoted him to Administrator of Jingzhao; he did not go, was transferred to serve in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor faulted Liu Song for misapplying the law and demoted him to prefect of Jingzhao. Liu Song never took up that post and was reassigned instead to Henei.

sentences.zh: 臨發，上便宜，多所納用。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, he submitted convenient proposals, many of which were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out he offered practical policy recommendations, many of which the throne accepted.

sentences.zh: 郡界多公主水碓，遏塞流水，轉為浸害，頌表罷之，百姓獲其便利。

translations.literal: Within the commandery boundary were many princesses' water trip-hammers that dammed and blocked flowing water, turning into inundation harm; Song memorialized to abolish them, and the hundred surnames obtained their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Princess-owned water mills across the commandery had choked the streams and caused flooding. Liu Song had them shut down by edict, to the great relief of the commoners.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on account of mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除淮南相。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he was appointed Chancellor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning term ended he was named chancellor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 在官嚴整，甚有政績。

translations.literal: In office he was strict and orderly, and had very good administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He ran a tight administration and compiled an impressive record.

sentences.zh: 舊修芍陂，年用數萬人，豪強兼併，孤貧失業，頌使大小戮力，計功受分，百姓歌其平惠。

translations.literal: Formerly repairing Shao Lake annually used several tens of thousands of men; powerful families annexed labor, orphans and poor lost employment. Song caused great and small to join strength, reckoned merit and received shares, and the hundred surnames sang his even kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The old Shao Lake works had drafted tens of thousands each year while magnates monopolized labor and left widows and paupers destitute. Liu Song made every household share the burden by measured shifts and fair rationing, and the people praised his equity.

sentences.zh: 頌在郡，上疏曰：

translations.literal: When Song was in the commandery, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: While administering the commandery Liu Song memorialized as follows.

sentences.zh: 又論肉刑，見《刑法志》。

translations.literal: He also discussed mutilating punishments; see the Treatise on Punishments and Law.
translations.idiomatic: His further memorial on restoring mutilating punishments is recorded in the Treatise on Punishments and Law.

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「得表陳封國之制，宜如古典，任刑齊法，宜復肉刑，及六州將士之役，居職之宜，諸所陳聞，具知卿之乃心為國也。

translations.literal: An edict replied that the memorial on enfeoffment following ancient canons, on restoring corporal punishment to align the laws, on service obligations for the six provinces, and on tenure in office had all been received, and that the throne fully knew his heart was set on the good of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered that it had read his views on princely fiefdoms after the ancient pattern, on restoring corporal punishment to unify the law, on service obligations for the six provinces, and on tenure in office, and that in every point it saw how wholly he devoted himself to the realm.

sentences.zh: 動靜數以聞。」

translations.literal: Report your movements and decisions frequently to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the throne informed as matters develop.

sentences.zh: 元康初，從准南王允入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang, he followed Prince of Huainan Yun to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuankang era he accompanied Prince Yun of Huainan to the capital; the received text miswrites the river name Huai.

sentences.zh: 會誅楊駿，頌屯衛殿中，其夜，詔以頌為三公尚書。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Jun was executed; Song garrisoned and guarded inside the halls, and that night an edict made Song Masters of Writing for the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun was put to death Liu Song held the palace watch, and that same night the emperor named him director of the Three Excellencies section of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 又上疏論律令事，為時論所美。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a memorial discussing statutes and ordinances matters, and was praised by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: A further memorial on statutes and ordinances drew admiration across the court.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉吏部尚書，建九班之制，欲令百官居職希遷，考課能否，明其賞罰。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, establishing the nine-ranks system, wishing to cause the hundred officials in office to hope rarely for promotion, examine and assess ability or inability, and clarify their rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In time he became director of personnel and framed a nine-grade scheme meant to keep officials in post longer, grade their performance, and make rewards and sanctions transparent.

sentences.zh: 賈郭專朝，仕者欲速，竟不施行。

translations.literal: The Jia and Guo cliques monopolized court; office-seekers desired speed, and in the end it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: With the Jia and Guo factions dominating the government and every careerist demanding rapid promotion, the reform was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫之害張華也，頌哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao of Lun harmed Zhang Hua, Song wept for him very bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Lun of Zhao murdered Zhang Hua, Liu Song mourned him with wrenching grief.

sentences.zh: 聞華子得逃，喜曰：「茂先，卿尚有種也！

translations.literal: Hearing that Hua's son had been able to escape, he joyfully said: "Maoxian, you still have seed!
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhang Hua's son had escaped, he cried with relief, Maoxian, your line survives yet!

sentences.zh: 」倫党張林聞之，大怒，憚頌持正而不能害也。

translations.literal: " Lun partisan Zhang Lin heard it, was greatly angry, feared Song's upholding rectitude and could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin, a partisan of Prince Lun, heard this and fumed, yet dared not strike Liu Song down because his integrity commanded respect.

sentences.zh: 孫秀等推崇倫功，宜加九錫，百僚莫敢異議。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu and others extolled Lun's achievements and said the nine bestowals ought to be added; the hundred officials none dared a different opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu and his clique praised Prince Lun's merits and pressed for the nine insignia of usurpation, and not a minister dared dissent.

sentences.zh: 頌獨曰：「昔漢之錫魏，魏之錫晉，皆一時之用，非可通行。

translations.literal: Song alone said: "Formerly Han's bestowal on Wei, Wei's bestowal on Jin, were all one-time uses, not able to be generally applied.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song alone objected, The Han grant to Wei and the Wei grant to Jin were one-off expedients, not a precedent to repeat at will.

sentences.zh: 今宗廟乂安，雖嬖後被退，勢臣受誅，周勃誅諸呂而尊孝文，霍光廢昌邑而奉孝宣，並無九錫之命。

translations.literal: Now the ancestral temple is peaceful; although the favorite empress was dismissed and powerful ministers received execution, Zhou Bo executed the various Lus and honored Emperor Xiaowen, Huo Guang deposed Changyi and served Emperor Xiaoxuan—neither had orders of the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: The shrines are secure again: the favorite consort has been set aside and the overmighty ministers executed, as when Zhou Bo purged the Lü clan for Emperor Wen or Huo Guang deposed the king of Changyi for Emperor Xuan. Neither crisis was answered with the nine bestowals.

sentences.zh: 違舊典而習權變，非先王之制。

translations.literal: Violating old canons and practicing expedient shifts is not the former kings' system.
translations.idiomatic: To cast aside established rite and reach for such contrivances is alien to the way of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 九錫之議，請無所施。

translations.literal: As for the discussion of the nine bestowals, I request nothing be applied.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that the proposal for the nine bestowals be dropped entirely.

sentences.zh: 」張林積忿不已，以頌為張華之黨，將害之。

translations.literal: " Zhang Lin piled up resentment without cease, took Song as Zhang Hua's faction, and was about to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin nursed a growing grudge, branded Liu Song a partisan of Zhang Hua, and plotted to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 孫秀曰：「誅張、裴已傷時望，不可復誅頌。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu said: "Executing Zhang and Pei has already injured the age's expectation; we cannot again execute Song.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu warned him, Executing Zhang Hua and Pei Xiu has already cost us the goodwill of the realm. Liu Song must not be killed as well.

sentences.zh: 」林乃止。

translations.literal: " Lin then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 於是以頌為光祿大夫，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song was made Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, and pacing horses were set at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song was therefore appointed grand master of splendid carriage with the honor of dismounting rails before his gate.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒，使使者弔祭，賜錢二十萬、朝服一具，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill and died; envoys were sent to condole and sacrifice, granting two hundred thousand cash and one set of court dress; his posthumous name was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness. The court sent envoys to mourn him, gave two hundred thousand cash and a full set of court robes, and posthumously styled him Zhen, Upright.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎劉沈議，頌當時少輩，應贈開府。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentleman Liu Shen debated that Song, of the age's younger generation, ought to be posthumously gifted opening of a mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen of the palace secretariat argued that Liu Song, among the foremost men of his generation, deserved the posthumous privilege of a grand commander's establishment.

sentences.zh: 孫秀素恨之，不聽。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu long hated him and did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu, who had long detested Liu Shen, rejected the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 頌無子，養弟和子雍早卒，更以雍弟詡子𨻳為嫡孫，襲封。

translations.literal: Song had no sons; he had adopted his younger brother He's son Yong, who died early; he further took Yong's younger brother Xu's son Na as heir grandson, to inherit the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song left no sons. He had adopted Yong, son of his brother Liu He, but Yong died young, so the line passed to Na, son of Xu, Yong's younger brother, as heir grandson to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: ，詔以頌誅賈謐督攝眾事有功，追封梁鄒縣侯，食邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: , an edict because Song in executing Jia Mi and overseeing the multitude of affairs had merit, posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Liangzou county, with food households one thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict noted Liu Song's part in executing Jia Mi and steadying the government, posthumously creating him marquis of Liangzou with fifteen hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 頌弟彪字仲雅，參安東軍事。

translations.literal: Song's younger brother Biao, courtesy name Zhongya, was a staff adviser on Eastern Pacification military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song's younger brother Liu Biao, courtesy name Zhongya, served on the staff of the army of eastern pacification.

sentences.zh: 伐吳，獲張悌，累官積弩將軍。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Wu, he captured Zhang Ti, and by accumulated offices became General of the Crossbowmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Wu he took the Wu commander Zhang Ti prisoner and rose through several posts to general of the crossbowmen.

sentences.zh: 及武庫火，彪建計斷屋，得出諸寶器。

translations.literal: When the armory caught fire, Biao proposed a plan to cut off roofs, enabling the various precious implements to be brought out.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial armory burned, Liu Biao ordered sections of roof struck away so the stored weapons could be salvaged.

sentences.zh: 曆荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 次弟仲字世混，曆黃門郎、滎陽太守，未之官，卒。

translations.literal: The next younger brother Zhong, courtesy name Shihun, passed through Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Xingyang; before going to office, he died.
translations.idiomatic: The next brother, Liu Zhong, courtesy name Shihun, held appointments as gentleman of the yellow gate and prefect of Xingyang but died before he could assume the latter post.

sentences.zh: 初，頌嫁女臨淮陳矯，矯本劉氏子，與頌近親，出養于姑，改姓陳氏。

translations.literal: Initially, Song married a daughter to Chen Jiao of Linhuai; Jiao was originally a Liu clan son, close kin to Song, given out in adoption to an aunt, and changed surname to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Song had given a daughter in marriage to Chen Jiao of Linhuai. Chen Jiao was born a Liu, a near kinsman of Liu Song, but had been adopted by an aunt and took the Chen surname.

sentences.zh: 中正劉友譏之，頌曰：「舜後姚虞、陳田本同根系，而世皆為婚，禮律不禁。

translations.literal: Rectifier Liu You ridiculed it; Song said: "After Shun, Yao Yu and Chen Tian were originally the same root system, yet generations all made marriage; rites and statutes did not forbid.
translations.idiomatic: The local rectifier Liu You objected. Liu Song replied, The houses of Yao, Yu, Chen, and Tian stem from a single Shun-line ancestry, yet they have intermarried for generations without the code forbidding it.

sentences.zh: 今與此同義，為婚可也。

translations.literal: Now with this it is the same meaning; to make marriage is permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Our case falls under the same principle, so the match is lawful.

sentences.zh: 」友方欲列上，為陳騫所止，故得不劾。

translations.literal: " You was just about to list and report upward, but was stopped by Chen Qian, therefore was able to avoid impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu You was preparing a formal denunciation when Chen Qian intervened, so no charges were filed.

sentences.zh: 頌問明法掾陳默、蔡畿曰：「鄉里誰最屈？

translations.literal: Song asked law clerks Chen Mo and Cai Ji, saying: "In the village who is most wronged?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song asked his law clerks Chen Mo and Cai Ji, Who in our district has been wronged worst?

sentences.zh: 」二人俱云：「劉友屈。

translations.literal: " The two together said: "Liu You is wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Both answered, "Liu You."

sentences.zh: 」頌作色呵之，畿曰：「友以私議冒犯明府為非，然鄉里公論稱屈。

translations.literal: " Song changed color and shouted at them; Ji said: "You, by private discussion offending the enlightened prefect, was wrong, yet the village's public opinion calls him wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song flushed and rebuked them. Cai Ji ventured, "Liu You was wrong to press a private grudge against your honor, yet public opinion still calls him the injured party."

sentences.zh: 」友辟公府掾、尚書郎、黃沙御史。

translations.literal: " You was summoned as clerk in the princely offices, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and Cavalier Investigator at Huangsha.
translations.idiomatic: Liu You went on to serve as princely clerk, gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and cavalier investigator at the Huangsha prison.

sentences.zh: 李重

translations.literal: Li Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong.

sentences.zh: 李重字茂曾，江夏鐘武人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhong, courtesy name Maozeng, was a man of Zhongwu in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong, courtesy name Maozeng, was a native of Zhongwu in Jiangxia commandery.

sentences.zh: 父景，秦州刺史、都亭定侯。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Inspector of Qinzhou, Marquis Ding of Duting.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Jing had been inspector of Qinzhou and marquis Ding of Duting.

sentences.zh: 重少好學，有文辭；

translations.literal: Zhong in youth loved learning and had literary phrasing;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong loved learning from youth and wrote with polish;

sentences.zh: 早孤，與群弟居，以友愛著稱。

translations.literal: he was early orphaned, dwelt with his band of younger brothers, and was noted for friendly love.
translations.idiomatic: orphaned early, he kept house with his younger brothers and was famed for fraternal devotion.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為本國中正，遜讓不行。

translations.literal: At the capping age he became rectifier of his native state, declined yielding and did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: When capped he was offered the rectifier's post for his home principality but modestly refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 後為始平王文學，上疏陳九品曰：

translations.literal: Later he became literary scholar to Prince Shiping of the Wei, and submitted a memorial stating on the nine ranks:
translations.idiomatic: He later became tutor in letters to the prince of Shiping and memorialized on the nine-rank system as follows.

sentences.zh: 遷太子舍人，轉尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Household Gentleman to the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to household gentleman to the heir apparent and then to gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時太中大夫恬和表陳便宜，稱漢孔光、魏徐幹等議，使王公已下制奴婢限數，及禁百姓賣田宅。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Palace Grandee Tian He memorialized convenient matters, citing Han Kong Guang, Wei Xu Gan and others' debates, causing kings and dukes downward to regulate slave and maidservant limit numbers, and forbidding the hundred surnames to sell fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Palace Grandee Tian He then submitted a utilitarian memorial, invoking Han debates led by Kong Guang and Wei discussions by Xu Gan, urging caps on slaveholding for the nobility downward and a ban on commoners' sale of land and houses.

sentences.zh: 中書啟可，屬主者為條制。

translations.literal: The palace secretariat opened and approved, charging the competent authorities to make articles and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The palace secretariat endorsed the plan and told the responsible agencies to draft implementing rules.

sentences.zh: 重奏曰：

translations.literal: Zhong memorialized saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong replied in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 又司隸校尉石鑒奏，郁林太守介登役使所監，求召還；

translations.literal: Moreover Metropolitan Commandant Shi Jian memorialized that Administrator of Yulin Jie Deng had conscripted those he supervised, requesting recall;
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Commandant Shi Jian also charged Jie Deng, prefect of Yulin, with illegally drafting men under his supervision and asked that Deng be recalled.

sentences.zh: 尚書荀愷以為遠郡非人情所樂，奏登貶秩居官。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing Xun Kai thought distant commanderies were not what human feelings delighted in, and memorialized to demote Deng in rank while keeping him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Kai of the Masters of Writing argued that no one willingly took a distant post and proposed merely demoting Jie Deng in rank while leaving him in place.

sentences.zh: 重駁曰：「臣聞立法無制，所以齊眾檢邪，非必曲尋事情，而理無所遺也。

translations.literal: Zhong rebutted saying: "Your servant has heard that establishing law without caprice is the means to align the multitude and restrain wrongdoing; it is not necessary to bend to seek each circumstance, yet principle has nothing left out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong demurred, Law exists to hold the many to one standard and curb abuse, not to chase every special case while leaving justice undone.

sentences.zh: 故所滯者寡，而所濟者眾。

translations.literal: Therefore what is blocked is few, while what is aided is many.
translations.idiomatic: Clear rules snag few and help the many.

sentences.zh: 今如登郡比者多，若聽其貶秩居官，動為准例，懼庸才負遠，必有黷貨之累，非所以肅清王化，輯寧殊域也。

translations.literal: Now cases like Deng's commandery are many; if we listen to demoting him in rank while keeping office, moving to make it a standard precedent, I fear mediocre talents burdened with distance will necessarily have the trouble of bribery goods; this is not the means to clarify royal transformation and bring peace to distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: Remote posts like Yulin abound. If we treat a token demotion as precedent, every mediocre official banished to the marches will resort to graft. That will not purify government or pacify the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜聽鑒所上，先召登還，且使體例有常，不為遠近異制。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks it fitting to listen to what Jian submitted, first recall Deng, and moreover cause precedent to be constant, not making different systems for far and near.
translations.idiomatic: I urge acceptance of Shi Jian's memorial: recall Jie Deng at once and hold one rule for near and distant posts alike.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and issued an edict accordingly.

sentences.zh: 太熙初，遷廷尉平。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixi, he was promoted to Justice Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taixi era he was promoted to justice assessor in the commandant of justice's office.

sentences.zh: 駁廷尉奏邯鄲醉等，文多不載。

translations.literal: He rejected the commandant of justice's memorial on Handan Zui and others; the text largely does not record it.
translations.idiomatic: He overturned several commandant findings in cases such as Handan Zui; the full texts are omitted here.

sentences.zh: 再遷中書郎，每大事及疑議，輒參以經典處決，多皆施行。

translations.literal: Again he was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; whenever great matters and doubtful deliberations occurred, he always consulted the classics to decide them, and most were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: A second promotion brought him to gentleman of the palace secretariat. On great matters and doubtful points he habitually cited the classics in his rulings, and most of his opinions were adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書吏部郎，務抑華競，不通私謁，特留心隱逸，由是群才畢舉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Personnel Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, striving to suppress flashy competition, not granting private audiences, especially attending to recluses; thereby the host of talents was fully raised.
translations.idiomatic: As personnel gentleman of the Masters of Writing he curbed ostentatious rivalry, refused private solicitations, and sought out hidden talent until worthy men filled the ranks.

sentences.zh: 拔用北海西郭湯、琅邪劉珩、燕國霍原、馮翊吉謀等為秘書郎及諸王文學，故海內莫不歸心。

translations.literal: He raised and employed Beihai West Guo Tang, Langye Liu Hang, Yanguo Huo Yuan, Fengyi Ji Mou and others as secretariat gentlemen and various princes' literary scholars; therefore within the seas none did not turn hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Guo Tang of Beihai, Liu Hang of Langye, Huo Yuan of Yan, Ji Mou of Fengyi, and others to secretariat posts and princely tutorships, winning the loyalty of scholars everywhere.

sentences.zh: 時燕國中正劉沈舉霍原為寒素，司徒府不從，沈又抗詣中書奏原，而中書復下司徒參論。

translations.literal: At that time Yan state's rectifier Liu Shen recommended Huo Yuan as cold and plain; the Minister of Education office did not follow; Shen again resisted and went to the palace secretariat to memorialize Yuan, and the palace secretariat again sent down to the Minister of Education for joint discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shen, rectifier for Yan, nominated Huo Yuan for the cold-and-plain category, the ministry of education balked. Liu Shen appealed to the palace secretariat, which bounced the case back to the ministry for joint review.

sentences.zh: 司徒左長史荀組以為：「寒素者，當謂門寒身素，無世祚之資。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Left Chief Clerk Xun Zu thought: "Cold and plain ought to mean gate cold and person plain, without hereditary emolument's resources.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu, left chief clerk of the ministry of education, argued that cold-and-plain means humble birth and plain station, without inherited stipends.

sentences.zh: 原為列侯，顯佩金紫，先為人間流通之事，晚乃務學，少長異業，年逾始立，草野之譽未洽，德禮無聞，不應寒素之目。

translations.literal: Yuan was a ranked marquis, conspicuously wearing gold and purple; first he did human-world circulation matters, only later strove at learning; youth and maturity had different occupations; his years passed the first establishment; wilds' reputation had not reached everywhere; virtue and rites were unheard of—he should not answer to the label cold and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yuan is already a full marquis with gold seal and purple ribbon. He trafficked in worldly affairs in youth and turned to scholarship only late; he has passed thirty with no wide rural reputation and no renown for virtue or ritual. He does not fit the cold-and-plain rubric.

sentences.zh: 」重奏曰：

translations.literal: Zhong memorialized saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong answered in a further memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ruled in Li Zhong's favor.

translations.literal: Equals sign.
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted text here inserts a stray mark from the typesetting source.

sentences.zh: 李毅

translations.literal: Li Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi.

sentences.zh: =重與李毅同為吏部郎，時王戎為尚書，重以清尚見稱，毅淹通有智識，雖二人操異，然俱處要職，戎以識會待之，各得其所。

translations.literal: = Zhong together with Li Yi both were Personnel Ministry gentlemen; at the time Wang Rong was Director of the Masters of Writing; Zhong by pure high-mindedness was praised, Yi by broad penetration had wisdom and insight; although the two men's conduct differed, yet both occupied key posts, and Rong by discerning accord treated them, each obtaining his place.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong served alongside Li Yi as personnel gentleman while Wang Rong headed the Masters of Writing. Li Zhong was admired for austere integrity, Li Yi for encyclopedic wit. Though their temperaments differed, Wang Rong sized up each man and used him to best effect.

sentences.zh: 毅字茂彥，舊史闕其行事。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Maoyan, the old histories lack his deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, courtesy name Maoyan, left so slight a record that older histories omit his career.

sentences.zh: 于時內官重，外官輕，兼階級繁多，重議之，見《百官志》。

translations.literal: At that time inner officials were heavy, outer officials light, and moreover ranks and grades were numerous; Zhong debated them; see the Treatise on Officials.
translations.idiomatic: At that time inner-court posts outweighed local office and rank titles had proliferated wildly. Li Zhong's critique is preserved in the Treatise on Officials.

sentences.zh: 又上疏曰：「凡山林避寵之士，雖違世背時，出處殊軌，而先王許之者，嘉其服膺高義也。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a memorial saying: "As for gentlemen who avoid favor in mountains and forests, although they violate the age and turn their backs on the times, emerging and resting follow different tracks, yet the former kings permitted them, praising their embracing high righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, Recluses who flee the court to the hills may shun the age, yet the sage-kings honored them for clinging to a higher duty than office.

sentences.zh: 昔先帝患風流之弊，而思反純樸，乃諮詢朝眾，搜求隱逸。

translations.literal: Formerly the late emperor worried over the fashionable current's harms, and thought to return to pure simplicity, then consulted the court multitude and searched for reclusion.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor grew alarmed at fashionable excess and sought to restore plain virtue, he polled the court and summoned recluses.

sentences.zh: ，始以太子中庶子征安定皇甫謐，四年又以博士征南安朱沖，，復以太子庶子征沖，雖皆以病疾不至，而朝野悅服。

translations.literal: First with Heir Apparent Palace Attendant he summoned Anding Huangfu Mi; in the fourth year again with erudite he summoned Nan'an Zhu Chong; again with Heir Apparent Attendant he summoned Chong; although all because of illness did not arrive, yet court and wilds were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He first called Huangfu Mi of Anding with the title attendant of the heir apparent's household, then in the fourth year summoned Zhu Chong of Nan'an as a court erudite, and later summoned Zhu Chong again as heir apparent's attendant. Both men pleaded illness and stayed home, yet the gesture won acclaim at court and in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 陛下遠邁先帝禮賢之旨，臣訪沖州邑，言其雖年近耋耋，而志氣克壯，耽道窮藪，老而彌新，操尚貞純，所居成化，誠山棲耆德，足以表世篤俗者也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty far surpasses the late emperor's intent to treat worthies with ritual; your servant has inquired of Chong in his commandery, and they say that although his years are near aged-aged, yet his will and qi are able to be strong, addicted to the Way in poor wilds, old yet more new, conduct and esteem chaste and pure, where he dwells becomes transformation—truly a mountain-dwelling aged virtue, enough to display the age and thicken custom.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty exceeds even Emperor Wu's reverence for recluses. I have asked about Zhu Chong in his home commandery: though he is in his eighties his spirit is vigorous, he pursues the Way in the depths of the wilds with growing zeal, and his life chastens every village he touches. He is a sage of the hills who could edify the age.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜垂聖恩，及其未沒，顯加優命。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks it fitting to let sagely grace fall, while he has not yet perished, clearly adding excellent appointment.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to show him imperial favor while he still lives and grant him a distinguished summons.

sentences.zh: 」時朝廷政亂，竟不能從。

translations.literal: At that time the court's government was chaotic, and in the end could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court was in turmoil and never acted on the proposal.

sentences.zh: 出為行討虜護軍、平陽太守，崇德化，修學校，表篤行，拔賢能，清簡無欲，正身率下，在職三年，彈黜四縣。

translations.literal: He went out as acting General Who Punishes the Caitiffs and Protects the Army and Administrator of Pingyang, exalted virtue transformation, repaired schools, memorialized earnest conduct, raised worthy ability, was pure and simple without desire, rectified his person to lead those below; in office three years, he impeached and dismissed four counties.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as acting general who punishes the caitiffs and army protector and as prefect of Pingyang, where he promoted moral education, rebuilt schools, cited men of proven integrity, promoted talent, lived plainly without private wants, and set a personal example for subordinates. Within three years he had four magistrates removed for cause.

sentences.zh: 弟嶷亡，表去官。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi died; he memorialized to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Yi died he resigned by memorial.

sentences.zh: 永康初，趙王倫用為相國左司馬，以憂逼成疾而卒，時年四十八。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongkang, Prince Zhao of Lun employed him as Left Major to the Chancellor of State; because worry and pressure became illness he died, at the time age forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongkang era Prince Lun of Zhao named him left major to the chancellor of state. Anxiety and intimidation broke his health, and he died at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 家貧，宅宇狹小，無殯斂之地，詔於典客署營喪。

translations.literal: The family was poor, the house narrow and small, without ground for laying out the bier; an edict ordered mourning arranged at the Reception of Guests office.
translations.idiomatic: His family was destitute and his house too small for the funeral rites, so the court ordered the reception office to host the obsequies.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was gifted Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; his posthumous name was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and the posthumous name Cheng, Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 子式，有美名，官至侍中，咸和初卒。

translations.literal: His son Shi had a fair reputation, his office reached Palace Attendant, and he died at the beginning of Xianhe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Shi enjoyed a fine reputation, rose to palace attendant, and died early in the Xianhe era.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: Historical evaluation bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial rubric: historical judgment.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：子雅束發登朝，竭誠奉國，廣陳封建，深中機宜，詳辨刑名，該核政體。

translations.literal: The historian says: Ziya, binding hair ascending court, exhausted sincerity serving the state, broadly stated enfeoffment, deeply hit opportune fitness, in detail discriminated punishments and names, comprehensively examined the polity's substance.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write that from the day Liu Song bound up his hair for office he served the state with utter loyalty, laid out far-reaching plans for feudal enfeoffment that struck the heart of the matter, and dissected penal law and administrative structure with exhaustive care.

sentences.zh: 雖文慚華婉，而理歸切要。

translations.literal: Although his writing was ashamed compared to flowery grace, yet principle returned to cutting essentials.
translations.idiomatic: His prose may lack literary polish, yet his reasoning always drives to the crux.

sentences.zh: 游目西京，望賈誼而非遠；

translations.literal: Roaming eyes over the Western Capital, gazing at Jia Yi and not being far;
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the Western Han capital he stands within sight of Jia Yi.

sentences.zh: 眷言東國，顧郎顗而有餘。

translations.literal: Turning words to the eastern state, regarding Lang and Yi yet having surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the scholars of the eastern heartland, he matches the stature of men such as Lang Yi with room to spare.

sentences.zh: 逮元康之間，賊臣專命，舉朝戰慄，苟避菹醢；

translations.literal: By the time of the Yuankang years, traitor ministers monopolized commands; the whole court trembled with fear, merely avoiding mincemeat;
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuankang years, when usurping ministers held absolute power and the whole court cowered merely to escape the chopping block.

sentences.zh: 頌以此時，忠鯁不撓，哭張公之非罪，拒趙王之妄錫，雖古遺直，何以尚茲。

translations.literal: at this time Song, loyal and blunt, was not bent; he wept at Lord Zhang's lacking crime, refused Prince Zhao's reckless bestowal—even ancient leftover straightness, how could it surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song alone remained bluntly loyal: he mourned Zhang Hua's innocence and rejected Prince Lun's illicit honors. The straight-speaking worthies of antiquity could scarcely better him.

sentences.zh: 至於緣其私議，不平劉友，異夫憎而知善，舉不避仇者歟！

translations.literal: As for following his private debate, not being fair to Liu You—is this different from hating yet knowing the good, raising without avoiding enemies!
translations.idiomatic: Yet when private pique led him to wrong Liu You, he fell short of the ideal that hates the sin yet knows the good and recommends even a foe!

sentences.zh: 李重言因革之理，駁田產之制，詞愜事當，蓋亹癖可觀。

translations.literal: Li Zhong spoke on following and changing's principle, rebutted field and property regulations; words matched affairs fittingly—his diligent earnestness was worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong expounded the logic of continuity and reform and demolished unsound rules on land and property; his language fit the facts, and his tireless precision repays reading.

sentences.zh: 及銳志銓衡，留心隱逸，浚沖期之識會，豈虛也哉！

translations.literal: When he sharpened his will on personnel evaluation and attended to reclusion, Rong's expectation of discerning accord—how could it be empty!
translations.idiomatic: When he turned his keen mind to appointments and to recluses, he vindicated Wang Rong's trust in his discernment—that reputation was no empty boast!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：劉頌剛直，義形於詞。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Liu Song was firm and straight; righteousness took form in his words.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: Liu Song was unbending, and righteousness shaped every word he spoke.

sentences.zh: 自下摩上，彼實有之。

translations.literal: From below rubbing upward—he truly had it.
translations.idiomatic: He dared remonstrate upward against power, and he meant every word.

sentences.zh: 李重清雅，志乃無私。

translations.literal: Li Zhong was pure and elegant; his intent then was without selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong was refined and disinterested, and his aims were never self-serving.

sentences.zh: 推賢拔滯，嘉言在茲。

translations.literal: Pushing worthies and raising the stuck—fine words are here.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the worthy and freed the blocked; here lies his lasting counsel.

sentences.zh: 懋哉兩哲，邦家之基。

translations.literal: Admirable, the two wise men—foundations of state and family.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid were these two sages, true foundations of the house of Jin.
